title: oncall-optimizer-sequencer-and-silent-debounce
author: Priya Kothari
release_notes: Adds on-call playbook sequencing, conflict autocorrection, and silent debounce windows to reduce pager noise. Backwards compatible with existing playbook YAML; opt-in via incident-bot config flags. Includes metrics for deprecated playbook collisions and oncall-suppressed events.
description:
Motivation: On-call teams see frequent duplicate or conflicting automatic playbook triggers during multi-service incidents. That leads to noisy pagers, duplicated work, and occasional race conditions when multiple runbooks try to act concurrently. This PR introduces an "oncall optimizer" that deterministically sequences competing playbook actions and a lightweight "silent debounce" window to suppress rapid-fire automated escalations.

Design summary: Implement a sequencing layer inside incident-bot that: 1) assigns a deterministic order to candidate playbook runs using a stable hash of (incident_id, service, rule_priority, timestamp_bucket); 2) evaluates simple conflict predicates (resource lock, overlapping mitigation targets) and rewires lower-priority actions to delayed/no-op outcomes; 3) establishes a configurable silent debounce window per-service that suppresses non-critical automatic escalations for a short period after an initial mitigation attempt. The sequencing algorithm is intentionally conservative and synchronous in the controller to minimize surprises.

Key features and behaviors: - Deterministic sequencer: ensures same ordering across restarts within a short time-bucket. - Conflict autocorrector: if two playbooks would modify the same resource (e.g., routing table), the sequencer marks the lower-priority action as deferred and surfaces a single combined action to responders. - Silent debounce: low-confidence automated escalations are suppressed for a configurable window (default 90s) after a mitigation attempt; suppression events are emitted to metrics. - Local dry-run simulator: CLI mode `incident-bot simulate-sequence` validates a set of active rules against a sample incident to preview ordering and suppression decisions. - Telemetry: new metrics incidentbot.playbook.sequenced_count, incidentbot.playbook.suppressed_count, incidentbot.playbook.deferred_actions and tracepoints for sequencing decisions.

Files changed (high-level): - controller/sequencer.py: new sequencer and conflict resolution engine. - controller/simulator.py: local simulation CLI and unit harness. - config/defaults.yaml: added sequencer and debounce configuration knobs. - telemetry/metrics_registry.py: metrics registration and export hooks. - tests/test_sequencer.py: unit tests covering ordering, conflict cases, and debounce behavior. - cli/commands.py: added simulate-sequence command and flags. - docs/operational/playbook-sequencer.md: usage, tuning guide, and migration notes.

Commits (summary): - Add deterministic hashing and sequencing core (Priya K.) - Implement conflict autocorrector and resource lock model (Alex P.) - Add silent debounce implementation and config knobs (Miguel T.) - Add simulate-sequence CLI with sample fixtures (Priya K.) - Wire telemetry and dashboards (Rina S.) - Tests, docs, and release notes (Priya K.)

Testing and CI: - Extensive unit tests added (test coverage + sequencer edge cases). - Integration smoke test run in CI (incident-bot/integration/seq-smoke) flaked once on first run; fixed race by adding short randomized jitter and re-ran. - CI status: all checks passed after second run.

Review conversation (highlights): - Alex Park: "Please ensure sequencing does not increase mean response latency for high-priority actions; recommend a fast-path bypass for priority >= 100." Author reply: "Added bypass for priority >= 100 in the sequencer pipeline; documented behavior and tests added." - Miguel Torres: "Need visibility when two playbooks are merged into one action so responders can audit decisions." Author reply: "Added structured tracepoint 'sequencer.merge' and emitted a human-readable summary to the incident timeline when a merge happens." - Rina Shah: "How do we prevent deadlocks when two sequencers run concurrently in multi-controller setups?" Author reply: "Sequencer uses optimistic locking with a short lease and falls back to delay+retry; added a sim test that reproduces and verifies safety."

Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind incident-bot.sequencer.enabled (default false). - Canary rollout to 10% of customers for 48 hours with increased logging and telemetry. - If telemetry shows suppressed_count/spike in deferred actions but no errors, expand to 50% for 72 hours. - Full rollout only after no regressions in latency SLOs and positive pager noise reduction signal.

Migration notes and compatibility: - Existing playbook YAML files are unchanged; sequencing is opt-in. - Customers that rely on side-effect ordering should test with simulate-sequence. - The sequencer may alter the observed execution order of automatic actions; manual escalations are not affected.

Observability and dashboards: - New Grafana panels for sequenced_count, suppressed_count, and average debounce window per-service. - New alert: incidentbot.sequencer.error_rate > 0.5% for 10m triggers an investigation runbook.

Security and safety: - No privileged credentials introduced. - The conflict autocorrector intentionally avoids destructive merges; if uncertainty > threshold, action is deferred and a human hook is created.

Conclusion: This PR reduces noisy duplicate automations and prevents simple action collisions by providing a deterministic sequence and suppression semantics. It is conservative, opt-in, and accompanied by simulation tooling and telemetry to enable safe rollouts.
